failure_modes: Temporal-attention edit (C008-C011) reweights observed-node attention using a non-monotone contrast; over part of the window it would displace surrounding coordinates opposite to the static shape_yy/shape_xx endpoint contrast, degrading the primary affinity signal.

Dose edits (C001-C003) rescale an already RMS-normalized endpoint-VJP force without evidence of a directional benefit, risking unnecessary coordinate displacement and cumulative-RMS budget consumption.
Teacher-count edits (C005-C007) change only the number of detached nearest-k teachers and are not supported by any endpoint-contrast evidence as improving the shape_yy/shape_xx signal.
No decoded terminal labels or current-study outcome data are supplied, so no edit can be credited with final affinity benefit; last-record or survival credit is not final affinity.
result.rationale: D1.2: The registered temporal alternatives (C008 temporal_region_index, C009-C011 temporal_teacher_blend) change regional attention at observed score nodes using the same static teachers; they do not change teacher coordinates and are not velocity forces. Analyst's temporal evidence (continuous:0, landmark_00_soft_mass with 4 sign changes, first_rate_z≈+9.3 vs last_rate_z≈-10.0, no accepted polynomial, extrapolation disallowed) supports only observed-node interpolation, not a constant rule over the full window. However, the endpoint-integrated contrasts that carry the strongest and most batch-consistent signal are static shape descriptors (shape_yy q≈1.5e-5, 0/14 positive batches; shape_xx q≈8e-4, 1/14 positive), and the incumbent already uses static teachers with teacher_neighbors=4 and pointcloud_delta_A=1.0. D4.1: The offered edits are dose (C001-C003 pointcloud_delta_A), static regional index (C004), teacher count (C005-C007), and temporal attention/blend (C008-C011). None of these is a coordinate-target change that the evidence shows would reduce the shape_yy/shape_xx endpoint contrast; the temporal recipes only reweight attention at observed nodes and the dose edits rescale an already-normalized endpoint-VJP force. The evidence therefore does not provide a defensible expected advantage over the incumbent, so I retain it. D4.2: Predicted failure of a temporal-attention edit (e.g., C010 blend=0.5): because the observed landmark contrast is non-monotone with large opposing first/last rates, a blended time-conditioned attention would displace surrounding coordinates in the wrong direction over part of the window, degrading the static shape_yy/shape_xx endpoint contrast that is the primary affinity-relevant signal, and could push cumulative RMS toward the 6.0 A constraint. This predicted unnecessary displacement of surrounding coordinates is why I do not select a temporal or dose edit. Temperatures are immutable and were not proposed.
